finding.claim: On Cloud Foundry, actuator endpoints mapped at the plain /actuator route skip the CF permission check (RequiredPermissions), so env, heapdump, threaddump, and loggers POST are reachable unauthenticated when exposed.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP request to /actuator/{env,heapdump,threaddump,loggers} on CF (E1)
finding.sink: Endpoint handlers: EnvironmentEndpointOptions.cs:16 (Full), HeapDumpEndpointOptions.cs:14 (Full), ThreadDumpEndpointOptions.cs:14 (Full), LoggersEndpointMiddleware.cs:26-51

trace.note: Non-CF middlewares mapped under plain /actuator route on all platforms, including CF
CF route /cloudfoundryapplication also mapped; this is the only permission-gated copy
InvokeAsync calls CanInvoke(path)
Non-CF path returns isEnabled && isExposed; no permission check
CF permission check runs only when path starts with /cloudfoundryapplication, so /actuator requests are never checked

finding.guards_checked: Exposure check (EndpointOptionsExtensions.cs:21-42) enforced; verb, content-type and accept checks (EndpointMiddleware.cs:55-86) enforced; RequiredPermissions check absent on the plain route. Design intent not confirmed: no in-repo doc or test found stating plain /actuator is intentionally ungated on CF.

finding.claim: Decrypted config secrets are written to logs in plaintext at Trace level, violating the org policy against logging secrets at any level.
finding.source: Any config value of the form {cipher}... (E12)
finding.sink: LogDecrypt call logging PlainTextValue at DecryptionConfigurationProvider.cs:43, message template at line 58-59

trace.note: CipherRegex match on config value
Decrypt cipher text
LogDecrypt(key, value, decryptedValue) emits plaintext secret
LoggerMessage defined at Trace level with PlainTextValue parameter

finding.guards_checked: Regex timeout set (line 16). No check on log level or redaction of decryptedValue before logging. Exploitable only where Trace logging is enabled for this category.

finding.claim: Negative key cache is keyed on the attacker-controlled kid, so each unique kid in an unauthenticated JWT triggers a fresh synchronous outbound JWKS fetch, enabling resource exhaustion and request amplification to the IdP.
finding.source: Unauthenticated Bearer JWT with a unique kid header (E9)
finding.sink: Synchronous JWKS HTTP fetch FetchKeySet at TokenKeyResolver.cs:106-111 (GetAwaiter().GetResult())

trace.note: IssuerSigningKeyResolver invoked with keyId from token
ResolveSigningKey(options.Authority, keyId, Backchannel)
CachingResolveSigningKey; cache miss for new kid
Cache key is tokenKeysUri:keyId, so negative cache is per kid
FetchKeySet performs blocking outbound HTTP for every miss

finding.guards_checked: Authority comes from configuration (no attacker-controlled key URL). Audience and issuer validation applied (PostConfigureJwtBearerOptions.cs:34-61). Negative TTL 30-60s (lines 18-19, 78-79) does not bound distinct kids. OpenIdConnect TokenKeyResolver.cs has the same structure (lines 36, 43, 57, grep-confirmed, not read in full).

finding.claim: Config-server endpoints and credentials are taken from Eureka instance metadata with no trust check, so an attacker who can register an instance can supply a config source and credentials, injecting configuration into the app. Precondition: the attacker can register an instance under the config-server service ID.
finding.source: Eureka registry entry metadata password, user, configPath (E8)
finding.sink: Config server URI list and credentials applied to options and config data, then fetched by DoLoadAsync

trace.note: UpdateDiscoveryAsync takes all discovered instances
Instance metadata password read and used as credentials
Instance metadata configPath appended to URI
Combined URI list stored as last discovery result
Password from discovery applied to client options
Discovered password copied into config data

finding.guards_checked: No validation that discovered instances are trusted config servers. Registry trust is treated as a design assumption; this finding depends on that trust boundary.
